subject: vanguard satellite
title: The Oldest Satellite in Orbit Launched in 1958 and Stays Up Until 2198

scenes.text: The oldest thing humans ever put in space is still up there.
Vanguard 1. Launched March 17, 1958: a 1.5 kilogram sphere the size of a grapefruit. Khrushchev called it the grapefruit satellite.
Six solar cells made it the first solar-powered satellite. It fell silent in 1964. It did not fall down.
Sixty-eight years later it still circles Earth every 134 minutes, between 650 and nearly 4,000 kilometers up. More than 235,000 orbits by 2018.
Engineers once expected it to stay up 2,000 years. The thin upper air drags on it more than they thought. The estimate is now about 240.
It comes down around the year 2198. Until then, the oldest human-made object in space is a grapefruit from 1958.

description:
The oldest human-made object still in orbit is a grapefruit-sized satellite launched in 1958.
Vanguard 1 weighed about 1.5 kg and was the first satellite powered by solar cells; its transmitter went quiet in 1964, but the satellite has kept circling Earth every 134 minutes, between about 650 and 3,970 km up, with more than 235,000 orbits logged by its 60th birthday. Early estimates gave it 2,000 years aloft; atmospheric drag turned out to be stronger, and it is now expected to re-enter around 2198.
What would you want to be the last thing left of our era in orbit?
first_comment: Vanguard 1 proved Earth is slightly pear-shaped, just by how its orbit wobbled. What's the oldest piece of technology you still use?
